title: the four ways a turn must not break
intent: A turn that hangs is worse than a turn that fails: the person sits in front of an Emacs that no longer answers, and the journal stops telling them anything. Four classes of failure were reachable — a malformed argument container, a handler that signals, a callback that arrives twice, and a handler that returns nothing — and each of them could leave the run without a terminal state. This wave is the discipline of settling: every call reaches exactly one terminal result, every result the model sees is a string or a structured error, and every one of those four classes has a test that goes red when the guard is removed.
objection: Guards that catch everything catch nothing. A scheduler that normalises every failure into the same string has made the failure invisible, and the person reading the journal learns less than before.
refuted_by: A tool that returns nil, a handler that signals, and a callback that fires twice — all three in one batch. If the journal does not show three distinct terminal results, the guards are decoration.
